sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A website for finishing the book
sections.para: Dinis wants one environment to review and finish Generation Z Developers: the 2018 book in a repository as the first official version, working versions in a public vault, deltas between versions, the book as a graph at every altitude, voice comments, agents in roles, research, and the OpenRouter key kept in a separate private vault. The book's last part explains how it was built.

sections.label: In short
sections.para: The site is gen-z-developers.sgit.ai. The repository holds official versions, starting with 2018; a public vault holds working ones; each version gets a delta. The book becomes a graph at every altitude with infographics, reviewed by voice and by editor, copywriter and publisher agents. The OpenRouter key needs its own private vault.

sections.label: Why a website
sections.line: The best of the repositories, in one place
sections.para: The site gathers the best of what the project's repositories have built into one productive environment for reviewing the book. Many concepts first appeared on graphs.sgit.ai: a versioned shelf, seven roles with a folder each, the book as a graph, and the same book at several altitudes.

sections.label: The name
sections.line: An address that matches the book
sections.para: The printed cover says Gen Z Developers and the book is Generation Z Developers, so the site should be gen-z-developers.sgit.ai rather than a shorter form.

sections.label: The repository and the vault
sections.line: Official versions in Git, working ones in a vault
sections.para: The 2018 book is already final, so it goes into the repository as released and the site's first version shows exactly that. All later work happens in the vault, and a version moves into the repository when ready, with a delta against the previous one, brutal from 2018 to 2026 and precise after that, like the publishers page's versions.

sections.label: The book as a graph, at every altitude
sections.line: The book as a graph, at every altitude
sections.para: The book becomes a semantic graph with ontology and taxonomy. The graphs books tried an altitude ladder, the same book at five levels; this book should have that from the start, with an infographic at each: the whole book on a page, each part, each chapter, each area of the graph. A narrative path guides the reader, almost like a plot.

sections.label: Reading, reviewing, signing off
sections.line: Voice, boards and agents who challenge
sections.para: While reviewing, Dinis needs voice comments attached to sections, comments, a board and issues, and agents in roles, an editor, copywriter and publisher, who read, challenge and write interview scripts for him, as for ten hard questions for RiskMandate. Parts can be signed off. Everything is public; working data starts in the vault.

sections.label: Research and evidence
sections.line: Research and evidence for every section
sections.para: Around the text run agentic tasks: market research on readers, validation of claims, evidence behind each, and maps and graphs per section and eventually per paragraph, so the book can show its work as the newsroom's articles do.

sections.label: The OpenRouter key needs its own vault
sections.line: The OpenRouter key cannot go in the public vault
sections.para: The memo put the OpenRouter key in the book's vault, but that vault's read key will be published, so anything in it is readable by everyone. The key goes in a separate private vault opened only by Dinis's passkey, with a credit limit set at OpenRouter so a mistake costs little.

sections.label: The last part of the book
sections.line: How it was built, and ideas that held
sections.para: The book's last part should explain how the repository, vault, graph, altitudes, agents and versions come together, because that is what a Generation Z developer should be able to build. Dinis argues the first book's core ideas were universal, and that those who read and acted on it in 2018 were well prepared for the AI revolution.

sections.label: The brief
sections.para: The build brief is a public note, a website to finish the book, also on the briefs page; the book's plan is in Generation Z Developers (AI edition).

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: Nothing is built. The address is a proposal to confirm. The altitude ladder worked once, for one book on graphs.sgit.ai. And the claim that 2018 readers were well prepared is Dinis's argument, not a measured result.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: From Dinis's voice memo of 18 October 2026, graphs.sgit.ai's books, altitude ladder and roles, and the versions of the page for publishers. Related articles cover the book's plan, versions of versions, the graphs books, keys with credit limits and a book for one reader.
